correctness.rationale: The unique-response rule implies that strong vertices are pairwise at distance at least three. Crown graphs have only three possible sizes for this set: zero, one, or a deleted matched pair. In each case the unique-response and strong-Roman conditions force every remaining label and the defender strength. The resulting three families are exhaustive. A standalone exhaustive verifier directly checks every permitted labeling for n=3 through 5.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The general 2-packing theorem can be specialized to recover the minimum after the crown 2-packings are analyzed, but it does not state or count all feasible URStRDFs. The accepted claim strengthens this to an exact three-family classification and complete weight enumerator.

value.rationale: The theorem gives a complete weight enumerator and all feasible functions for an established defensive graph parameter on a standard family. It also reveals a structural edge-deletion effect relative to complete bipartite graphs: the deleted matching creates the only nontrivial two-vertex 2-packings, which exactly index all minima and collapse the feasible family to linear size.
